subject: general
question: When was "Food for Work" programme first launched in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1977.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India launched the Food for Work Program'( FWP) in April 1977.**
 
• The **program is open to all Indian poor **who are ready to do homemade unskilled labour work and are in the need of pay envelope employment. 
 
• It's enforced as a **centrally- patronized scheme. **
 
• The program has ago been contained in the **National Rural Employment Guarantee Act( NREGA) of 2005** which has come into force in 200 linked sections of the country including **150 NFFWP sections.**
 
• **MGNREGA **is now the principal right-grounded employment guarantee scheme. 
 
• The **National Food for Work program was intermingled with NREGA latterly. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Latterly** in 2006,** the **Food for Work Program** got intermingled with **Mahatma Gandhi's National Rural Employment Guarantee Act** with numerous changes in policy enactment, perpetration, and control. 
 
• Presently, the F**ood for Work Programme **is one and the same part of**(the MGNREGA) Act,** M**ahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Act, which guarantees the “ right to work ” and ensures a minimum of 100 days of work for the pastoral poor as livelihood security. **
